title: How to Calculate Your Gross Annual Salary from an Hourly Rate (38-Hour Week)
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to a gross annual salary using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes tax, super, and award rate guidance.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week over 52 weeks, your gross annual salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours.

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage in Australia from 1 July 2026?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $33.05 per hour for casual employees including 25% loading. For a 38-hour week, that's $1,004.90 per week or $52,254.80 per year before tax.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my gross annual salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross annual salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

faqs.q: What tax will I pay on my gross annual salary in 2026-27?
faqs.a: For 2026-27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Plus a 2% Medicare levy generally applies.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to a Gross Annual Salary

If you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your **gross annual salary** by multiplying that rate by the number of hours you work each week and then by 52 weeks. This is the standard formula used across Australian payroll and is the basis for most full-time employment calculations.

### The 38-Hour Week Assumption

A full-time employee in Australia is generally expected to work 38 hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Act and most modern awards. When you use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, we assume a 38-hour week unless you tell us otherwise. This means the standard multiplier for a full-time gross annual salary is:

**Hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks = gross annual salary**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Using the formula:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year

This figure is the gross amount before tax and any deductions. It matches the weekly minimum of $1,004.90 published by the Fair Work Ombudsman for a 38-hour week.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australian employers pay their staff fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly amount:

**Hourly rate × 38 hours × 2 = gross fortnightly pay**

Using the minimum wage example:

$26.44 × 38 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight

This is useful when comparing salary offers or checking your payslip. You can also use our [the timesheet](/) to track your hours and see your estimated gross pay for any period.

## Different Rates for Different Jobs

Not everyone is paid the National Minimum Wage. Your minimum pay rate depends on the award or agreement that covers your job. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, which list the minimum hourly rates for each classification.

### Award Rates vs. Minimum Wage

Award rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, many awards have different pay levels for different skill grades. Always check your specific award to find your correct minimum rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool can help you identify the right award and rate.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a casual loading of 25% on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. The casual minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 + 25%).

When using our calculator, you should enter your base hourly rate and then select the casual loading checkbox. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool will add it for you. For more details, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions on top of your gross annual salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings. This means if your gross annual salary is $52,254.80, your employer will contribute an additional $6,270.58 into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

Super is not deducted from your pay – it is an extra cost for the employer. You can read more about how super interacts with your total remuneration on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Estimating Tax on Your Gross Annual Salary

Once you know your gross annual salary, you can estimate the tax you will pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of your taxable income. The Australian Taxation Office provides a gross pay estimator to help you work backwards from your net pay if needed.

For a full breakdown of what you might take home after tax, visit our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

## Average Earnings in Australia

For context, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported in May 2026 that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70. That equates to a gross annual salary of approximately $108,352.40 (using the 52-week multiplier). All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118.40 per year. These figures can help you see where your rate sits relative to the broader workforce. See our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

Always refer to the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for the latest official rates and consult a qualified professional for personal financial advice.
